intent: A record quiz with a misdirection: the counter runs to a number the modern hockey powers cannot touch, the THEN / NOW split sets six unbeaten golds against two recent bronzes, and the pin lands on the home town of the player they called the Wizard — a cricket country whose Olympic story is a stick and a ball.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Who has the MOST Olympic golds in men's field hockey?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Who has the most Olympic golds in men's field hockey?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: India. 8 Olympic golds in men's hockey, more than anyone.

lines.direction: ease back over the subcontinent; the Dutch flag-ball thinks on 'Netherlands'; a kangaroo sticker on 'Australia'; the golds counter runs 0 → 8 on 'total' with a stick sticker as India pulses
lines.text: The Netherlands and Australia are today's powers. Neither comes close to the total.

lines.direction: drift north toward the Gangetic plain; the SIX / BRONZE split lands on '6'; a flag-wave sticker on 'independence'; the Jhansi pin on 'Wizard' with a magic sticker as India pulses
lines.text: 6 came in a row, before and after independence, without losing a match, built around the man they called the Wizard.

lines.direction: tighten on the north; the 24–1 card on 'score' with a goal sticker; a snow sticker on 'Moscow'; the Indian flag-ball grins on 'Paris' as India pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: An early match against the United States produced a score never matched since. Gold last came in Moscow; bronze in Tokyo and Paris.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
